unit: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, to schoolteachers Walter and Bertha Shirley, who both died of fever shortly after her birth. Left an orphan, she spent her early childhood in poverty and hard labor caring for children for Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Hammond, followed by four months in an asylum. At age eleven, she was sent by mistake to Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, who had wanted a boy to help on the farm. Despite initial intentions to send her back, her vivid imagination and affectionate nature won over the siblings, and they decided to keep her. Anne settled into Avonlea, forming a deep 'bosom' friendship with Diana Barry and entering into a fierce academic rivalry with schoolmate Gilbert Blythe after he angered her by calling her 'Carrots.' She progressed rapidly in her studies under her teacher Miss Stacy, eventually attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, where she earned a First Class teacher's license and won the prestigious Avery Scholarship. Following the sudden death of Matthew Cuthbert and the failing eyesight of Marilla, Anne chose to give up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and care for Marilla. She took a position as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, where she successfully managed her pupils and founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. After two years of teaching, she reconciled her long-standing grudge against Gilbert Blythe, accepting his offer of friendship after he gallantly surrendered his post at the Avonlea school to her.
